[Evidence Lines] [143, 148, 149]
[Code Evidence] Line 143 calls av_calloc(stream_count, sizeof(StreamContext)) and assigns the result to nut->stream; the code only checks the return value with if (!nut->stream) and returns AVERROR(ENOMEM) on failure. If allocation succeeds, line 148 loops i from 0 to stream_count and line 149 calls avformat_new_stream(s, NULL) without checking the return value.
[Vulnerability Mechanism] avformat_new_stream returns NULL on allocation failure, but the return value is discarded at line 149, so no NULL check occurs and the caller continues as if a stream was created. If subsequent code dereferences the newly created stream (or the stream array) without verifying it, a NULL pointer dereference can occur. The code at lines 148-149 does not itself dereference the returned pointer, so the immediate unsafe consequence is an unchecked NULL return rather than a demonstrated dereference within these lines.
[Type Rationale] The unchecked return of avformat_new_stream at line 149 can yield a NULL pointer that is not validated before use, which is consistent with CWE-476 (NULL Pointer Dereference): the code expects a valid stream pointer but may proceed with NULL. The evidence supports the missing NULL check; the actual dereference would occur in downstream code not shown here.
[CWE Type] CWE-476

[Evidence Lines] [18, 19, 20, 21, 24, 25]
[Code Evidence] Line 18 clones inject_image into group4_image; lines 19-20 return MagickFalse without destroying group4_image when the clone fails. Line 21 calls ImageToBlob, producing an allocated buffer group4; lines 24-25 return MagickFalse without releasing group4 when ImageToBlob returns NULL.
[Vulnerability Mechanism] On the early-return error paths the function exits before freeing resources it had acquired: group4_image is leaked when CloneImage returns NULL, and the group4 buffer (when allocated) is leaked when ImageToBlob returns NULL, so allocated memory is never released after its effective lifetime.
[Type Rationale] The code fails to release allocated memory on error conditions, matching CWE-401's definition of not sufficiently tracking and releasing allocated memory after use, with the resulting resource-consumption/unavailability impact of a memory leak.
[CWE Type] CWE-401

[Evidence Lines] [11, 12, 13, 15, 16, 17, 18, 19, 23, 27, 32, 41, 47, 49, 55, 60, 67, 68, 77, 83, 85, 89, 94, 98, 99, 100, 101, 105, 111, 117, 125, 130, 143, 168, 179, 180, 181, 186, 192, 204, 211, 215]
[Code Evidence] msgUserState processes an attacker-supplied MumbleProto::UserState message. It checks presence flags (has_name, has_channel_id, has_mute/deaf/suppress/priority_speaker, has_comment, has_texture, has_user_id, has_self_deaf/self_mute/plugin_context/plugin_identity/recording) and applies permission checks, then uses message contents directly: msg.channel_id() is looked up via qhChannels.value (line 16), msg.texture() length is compared against iMaxImageMessageLength (line 68), msg.comment() is read and length-checked (lines 49, 55), msg.texture() is converted with blob() and passed to setTexture/hashAssign (lines 99-105), msg.plugin_context()/plugin_identity() are assigned to user fields (lines 126, 131), msg.recording() is assigned (line 169), and msg.channel_id() is passed to userEnterChannel (lines 180-181). Lines 204, 211, 215 read pDstServerUser->qbaTexture and hash fields during broadcast.
[Vulnerability Mechanism] The handler accepts client-controlled fields from the UserState message and only performs presence and permission checks; it does not validate the actual values (e.g., channel_id resolving to a valid/non-null channel, texture/comment sizes, plugin context/identity content, recording flag, session/actor fields). Several dereferences depend on those values: qhChannels.value(msg.channel_id()) may return null and is compared/used (lines 16-18), and userEnterChannel is called with that value (line 181). Missing value-level validation lets malformed or unexpected input reach processing paths that assume the data is well-formed.
[Type Rationale] The weakness matches CWE-20 because the code receives structured input (a protobuf message) and fails to validate required properties of that input (existence, size, consistency, domain conformance) before using it; the permission checks address authorization, not input validation, so the observed behavior is improper validation of attacker-controllable input as defined for CWE-20.
[CWE Type] CWE-20

[Evidence Lines] [22, 23, 24]
[Code Evidence] Line 22 calls sscanf with format "%*c%*c%u.%u.%u.%u%*c%3s%*c%u", supplying &ipaddr[0..3], protocol, and &port as output pointers. ipaddr is declared as guint ipaddr[4] and protocol is declared as char protocol[3+1]. The sscanf result is stored in fields_matched and later compared against 6.

The format string drives parsing of an externally supplied transport_info string, and the output pointers are the fixed-size arrays ipaddr and protocol. The code does not bound the number or size of conversions to the declared buffer capacities; the immediate unsafe consequence is that sscanf may write parsed values into these buffers beyond their intended capacity depending on the input and conversion behavior.
[Type Rationale] The vulnerable lines are the sscanf call and its output arguments, where parsed input is written through output pointers into fixed-size stack buffers. Writing past the end of those intended buffers matches CWE-787, which covers writing data past the end of the intended buffer; the code evidence supports a write-through-format-string mechanism rather than a read-only parsing issue.
[CWE Type] CWE-787

[Evidence Lines] [16, 17, 21, 22, 23, 25, 29, 33, 37, 41]
[Code Evidence] decode_preamble decodes fd_seg_cnt from the input pointer (line 15) and validates only that it is between 1 and CEPH_FRAME_MAX_SEGMENT_COUNT (lines 16-17). The loop at lines 21-23 writes desc->fd_lens[i] (ceph_decode_32) and desc->fd_aligns[i] (ceph_decode_16) for each of fd_seg_cnt entries. Lines 25, 29, 33, 37, and 41 read fd_lens[fd_seg_cnt - 1], fd_lens[0], fd_lens[1], fd_lens[2], and fd_lens[3] without any check that fd_seg_cnt is at least 4.
[Vulnerability Mechanism] The number of segment entries taken from the input controls the loop bound, but the fixed-size desc->fd_lens and desc->fd_aligns arrays are not checked against that count. If fd_seg_cnt exceeds the array capacity, the loop writes past the end of these arrays; if fd_seg_cnt is less than 4, the later fixed-index reads fd_lens[1], fd_lens[2], and fd_lens[3] also access beyond the initialized portion of the array. Both are missing size checks on input-derived indices.
[Type Rationale] The code copies input-derived values into fixed-size descriptor arrays without verifying that the number of entries fits the destination, which is the buffer-copy-without-input-size-check semantics of CWE-120. The out-of-bounds read at lines 25, 29, 33, 37, and 41 is a related but distinct consequence; CWE-120 is retained per the assigned label.
[CWE Type] CWE-120

[Evidence Lines] [6, 31]
[Code Evidence] Line 6 checks `if (!image) return;` but the loop at line 9 and the inner loop at line 14 are not guarded by this check, so execution can reach line 31 where `image[(row + j) * width + col + i + k]` is indexed and assigned to `ip`. [Type Rationale] The observed behavior matches CWE-476: a pointer (`image`) that the code expects to be valid is dereferenced while NULL, because the check at line 6 does not actually protect the dereference at line 31.

[Evidence Lines] [9, 33]

[Evidence Lines] [40, 92, 97]
[Code Evidence] Line 40 allocates a packet-scope buffer of linelen+1 bytes via tvb_memdup from tvb at offset and uses it as NUL-terminated text. Line 92 reads tvb bytes starting at offset+digest_type_len with length linelen-digest_type_len and passes them to hex_str_to_bytes. Line 97 copies digest_bytes->len bytes from digest_bytes->data into a DIGEST_LEN-byte buffer.
[Vulnerability Mechanism] linelen is the result of tvb_find_line_end and line 40 copies linelen+1 bytes; when the line-end search returns a length equal to the remaining tvb length without a trailing line terminator, the extra byte read at the end of the tvb can exceed the captured data. At line 92, digest_type_len is set from the matched prefix length (4, 5, 7, or 8) while linelen comes from the line-end search, so linelen-digest_type_len can exceed the bytes actually available after offset+digest_type_len, causing tvb_get_ptr to read past the end of the line/tvb region. At line 97, digest_bytes->len is only clamped by lines 94-95 after hex_str_to_bytes, and the memcpy uses digest_bytes->len as the copy length into a fixed DIGEST_LEN buffer, so if hex_str_to_bytes yields a length larger than DIGEST_LEN before the clamp, the copy reads beyond the intended digest buffer.
[Type Rationale] The unsafe operations are reads from tvb-backed buffers and a byte-array source using lengths that can exceed the available data, matching CWE-125's definition of reading data past the end of the intended buffer. The observations are limited to the shown length computations and copy/read calls; no out-of-bounds read is asserted for paths not evidenced by these lines.
[CWE Type] CWE-125

[Code Evidence] Line 19 sets ps_dec->u2_mb_x = u2_mb_addr_incr - 1, then line 20 clamps it to (ps_dec->u2_num_horiz_mb - 1). Lines 26-31 compare (ps_dec->u2_mb_x + u2_mb_addr_incr) against ps_dec->u2_num_horiz_mb and set u2_mb_addr_incr = ps_dec->u2_num_horiz_mb - ps_dec->u2_mb_x, then call impeg2d_dec_skip_mbs with (u2_mb_addr_incr - 1). [Vulnerability Mechanism] The macroblock address increment and motion type values are used to compute positions and indexes without sufficient validation against the buffer extents. The clamping at lines 20 and 29 does not guarantee that the subsequent skip count or the motion-type index stays within the intended bounds, so the derived index/count can select an out-of-range table entry or advance past the valid macroblock buffer, causing reads or writes outside the intended memory buffer.
[Type Rationale] The observed behavior is an operation on a memory buffer whose index or count is not properly restricted to the buffer's intended boundary, which matches CWE-119's definition of reading from or writing to a memory location outside the buffer's intended boundary.
[CWE Type] CWE-119

[Evidence Lines] [17, 23, 24, 29, 34]
[Code Evidence] av_bprint_get_buffer(bp, 1, &buf, &buf_size) obtains a buffer and its size; zstream.avail_out is set to buf_size; inflate writes output into buf; bp->len is advanced by zstream.next_out - buf; then bp->str[bp->len] = 0 writes a terminator at the new length.
[Vulnerability Mechanism] The output buffer size provided to inflate is buf_size, but the code assumes inflate will not write more than buf_size and then advances bp->len by the actual bytes written and appends a NUL at bp->str[bp->len]. If the buffer accounting or length tracking is inconsistent with the actual allocated buffer, the NUL termination at line 34 writes past the end of the intended buffer.
[Type Rationale] The unsafe behavior is a write beyond the end of an intended buffer (the NUL terminator at bp->str[bp->len] after length advancement), which matches CWE-787's definition of writing data past the end of the intended buffer. The evidence is limited to the buffer-length and termination operations shown; no other out-of-bounds mechanism is asserted.
[CWE Type] CWE-787

[Evidence Lines] [7, 9, 10, 11, 12]
[Code Evidence] Line 7 calls peek() and assigns its result to p without any NULL check. Lines 9 and 10 read Stack->next->type and Stack->next->val, dereferencing Stack->next. Lines 11 and 12 write Stack->next->type and Stack->next->val, again dereferencing Stack->next.
[Vulnerability Mechanism] The code dereferences pointers (the peek() return stored in p, and Stack->next) that it assumes are valid but does not verify are non-NULL. If peek() returns NULL or Stack->next is NULL, the subsequent accesses on lines 9-12 dereference a NULL pointer, causing undefined behavior such as a crash. The code provides no guards or error handling for these dereferences.
[Type Rationale] The observed behavior matches CWE-476: a pointer expected to be valid is dereferenced without a NULL check, leading to a NULL pointer dereference. The vulnerable lines perform dereferences of p and Stack->next without validating them first.
[CWE Type] CWE-476

[Evidence Lines] [163, 165, 166, 168, 169, 171, 172, 177, 179, 180]
[Code Evidence] In the LIT_CHAR_LOWERCASE_U case under RE_FLAG_UNICODE, line 163 checks `*re_ctx_p->input_curr_p == LIT_CHAR_LEFT_BRACE` and line 165 increments `input_curr_p`; lines 166-171 read hex digits via `lit_char_hex_to_int(*re_ctx_p->input_curr_p++)` in a loop bounded only by `input_curr_p < input_end_p`, accumulating `cp = cp * 16 + ...`; line 172 checks `cp > LIT_UNICODE_CODE_POINT_MAX` and raises a syntax error; lines 177-180 accept `LIT_CHAR_RIGHT_BRACE` and assign `re_ctx_p->token.value = cp`.
[Vulnerability Mechanism] The code reads and advances the input pointer while parsing a `\u{...}` escape, but the only value check is against LIT_UNICODE_CODE_POINT_MAX; nothing in the shown lines writes beyond a buffer, and no out-of-bounds write operation (array indexing store, memcpy, pointer store past end) appears in the annotated lines. The observed operations are bounded reads and a token value assignment, so the code as shown does not exhibit an out-of-bounds write.

The annotated lines show pointer advancement over the input buffer and scalar accumulation; no buffer store is present in the evidence, so the observed semantics do not support the CWE-787 write-past-end mechanism. This is a limitation of the supplied code/annotations rather than confirmation of the assigned type.
[CWE Type] CWE-787

[Evidence Lines] [120, 121, 122, 123, 124]
[Code Evidence] Lines 119-121 read a count via lsr_read_vluimsbf5 and allocate da->array.vals and da->array.units with gf_malloc. Lines 122-124 check for allocation failure and set lsr->last_error = GF_OUT_OF_MEM and return, without freeing the already-allocated sibling buffer.
[Vulnerability Mechanism] If one of the two gf_malloc calls fails, the function returns immediately after setting GF_OUT_OF_MEM. Any buffer allocated by the other successful gf_malloc call remains allocated with its pointer stored in da->array.vals or da->array.units, and is not released on this error path, leaking memory.
[Type Rationale] The code allocates memory and then takes an error return path without releasing the successfully allocated buffer, which matches CWE-401's missing release of memory after its effective lifetime, causing memory to remain unavailable for reuse.
[CWE Type] CWE-401

[Evidence Lines] [51, 82, 87]
[Code Evidence] Line 51 is a while loop driven by code = gif_get_code(fp, code_size, 0) that continues while the returned code is >= 0; line 82 is an inner while loop that walks code = table[0][code] while code >= clear_code; line 87 performs that table[0] lookup and only an equality check (code == table[0][code]) breaks the walk by returning 255.
[Vulnerability Mechanism] The LZW decode loops rely on gif_get_code eventually returning a negative value and on the table[0] predecessor chain eventually dropping below clear_code. If gif_get_code keeps returning non-negative codes, or if table[0] entries form a self-referential/cyclic chain, the loop conditions remain true and the loop cannot reach its exit; the code at line 87 only detects a direct self-reference, not longer cycles, so the exit at line 51 or 82 may never be reached.
[Type Rationale] This matches CWE-835 because the iteration has an exit condition that cannot be reached, leading to an infinite loop and resource consumption (CPU), consistent with the assigned CWE-835 definition.
[CWE Type] CWE-835

[Evidence Lines] [75, 79, 88]
[Code Evidence] Line 75 allocates a buffer sized by valuelen, which is derived from the on-disk attribute entry via be32_to_cpu(name_rmt->valuelen) at line 66; line 79 calls xfs_attr_rmtval_get(&args) to read the remote value; line 88 frees args.value via kmem_free only after the put_listent call at lines 82-87.
[Vulnerability Mechanism] The allocation size is controlled by an on-disk 32-bit attribute value length field without an explicit bound check in this function, so a crafted or corrupted attribute can cause a very large kmem_alloc of attacker-influenced size, consuming kernel memory; if the intervening calls return early (lines 80-81, 97-98), the allocated buffer is not freed, leaking the resource.
[Type Rationale] The code allocates a limited memory resource in an amount derived from untrusted on-disk metadata and can fail to release it on early return, matching CWE-400's uncontrolled allocation and maintenance of a limited resource leading to resource exhaustion.
[CWE Type] CWE-400

[Evidence Lines] [5, 20]

Line 20 passes the caller-supplied sound_model pointer from modelMemory->pointer() directly into mHwDevice->load_sound_model without any validation of the model contents beyond the NULL checks at line 8.

The code shown does not establish a concrete privilege-escalation or access-control-bypass path beyond this gating behavior.
[Type Rationale] The observed semantics involve a permission gate (captureHotwordAllowed) and the handling of an operation subject to access control, which aligns with the assigned category CWE-264 (Permissions, Privileges, and Access Controls). CWE-264 is a Category, not a specific weakness, so it cannot by itself pinpoint a single concrete mechanism; the code facts here only support that access control is exercised around loadSoundModel.
[CWE Type] CWE-264

[Evidence Lines] [14, 19]
